title: Edge Proxy Orchestration & Airlocked Upgrade Acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in strongly restricted/VPC environments ask for a deterministic, auditable way to perform control-plane and runtime upgrades without any continuous outbound egress. Many already use a local edge proxy or mirror in their DMZ. We need an acceptance contract and requirements for an orchestrated upgrade that leverages an on-prem edge proxy/mirror ("edge proxy orchestration") to safely stage, validate, and roll out operator and image changes in airlocked sites.
goals: Define minimal networking and orchestration controls, acceptance tests, and rollout windows so Private deployments can upgrade via staged mirror or operatorless bootstrap mechanisms while meeting zero-egress policies and SLAs for rollback and health recovery.
non_goals: Designing a new package distribution protocol from scratch or replacing customer-owned mirrors. Not covering cloud-hosted Dedicated flows.
success_metrics: 1) No customer-required outbound egress for upgrade path in >95% of tested cases. 2) Canary nodes report successful image + operator + KMS-rotated secret validation within 30 minutes in at least 90% of runs. 3) Mean time to detect (MTTD) upgrade drift < 5 minutes during staged window. 4) Rollback completes to previous known-good within SLA of 15 minutes for 95% of sites.
assumptions: Customers can provide a local edge proxy or mirror that supports TLS termination and signed artifact hosting. Site operators can run an on-site orchestrator (kube-operator or curated runbook). Bandwidth for staged delta sync is small but variable; large seeds may be delivered on removable media in extreme cases.
constraints: No permanent outbound egress allowed during upgrade; ephemeral outbound allowed only to pre-approved mirror seed push mechanisms under customer control. All artifacts must be signed and verifiable with customer KMS or provided public keys.
requirements_summary: 1) Staged artifact bundle format (manifest + signed blobs + delta patch). 2) Edge proxy handshake contract to fetch staged bundles using mutually authenticated TLS and mTLS where available. 3) Canary orchestration state machine: validate -> dry-run -> traffic-quiesce -> swap -> verify -> promote. 4) Operatorless bootstrap fallback for minimal operator surfaces. 5) Offline rollback and integrity verification steps. 6) Audit logs suitable for compliance export.
detailed_acceptance_criteria: - AC1: Artifact provenance. Every upgrade bundle must include a signed manifest (SHA256) and a signature verifiable with a provided public key; system refuses unsigned bundles. - AC2: Zero-egress validation. In a test harness, when site is configured in "no-egress" mode with only local mirror endpoints allowed, the upgrade completes end-to-end without any connection to external hosts (network flow capture demonstrates no outbound flows). - AC3: Canary thresholds. Canary population (configurable; default 3% of nodes, min 2) must report successful health checks for 15 minutes with no error rate >0.5% before broader rollout. - AC4: Bandwidth-tolerant delta sync. Large images are delivered as one-time seeded archive or streamed deltas; acceptance requires that syncs succeed over throttled links (down to 256kbps) within defined window for staged nodes. - AC5: KMS rotation and offline keys. Key rotation operations must succeed when KMS is provided via local HSM or customer KMS endpoint; when HSM is unreachable the system must allow manual key injection with operator audit trail. - AC6: Canaries under partition. Simulated partial-network partition tests (1 minute to 1 hour) must not leave nodes in inconsistent state; reconcile logic must detect divergence and either auto-rollback or quarantine per policy. - AC7: Observable proofs. Console/exportable playbook must include tokenized proof: artifact signature, fetch receipts, checksums, and operator approvals for each site.
implementation_notes: - Implement an upgrade controller that understands bundle manifests and staged rollout windows. - Leverage a plug-in edge-proxy adapter (Nginx/Caddy/Envoy) with mTLS and local filesystem cache. - Provide a lightweight 'bootstrap-agent' binary for sites without a functioning operator that can apply bundles via runbook steps and report status to control plane over an approved private channel. - Integrate with existing console telemetry and add a 'no-egress' test harness that can be run locally by SRE/support.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for manifest verification and signature validation. 2) Integration test: local mirror + private cluster upgrade simulation under normal bandwidth. 3) Chaos test: simulate intermittent partition and verify reconcile/rollback. 4) Performance test: delta sync under 256kbps link for 3 sequential upgrades. 5) Compliance test: export audit trail and ensure fields required for SOC2/ISO are present.
rollback_plan: - Pre-flight snapshot of control-plane resource manifests and image digests. - Canary rollback triggered automatically when error rate threshold exceeded or manually via console. - If operatorless bootstrap used, provide idempotent reverse-runbook that restores previous manifests and restarts services. - Post-rollback health check must be executed and logged within 10 minutes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer networks vary widely; edge proxies may be misconfigured. Mitigation: Provide a validation checklist and an automated liveness probe that runs pre-upgrade and verifies TLS/mTLS and filesystem write. Risk: Signed artifacts but key compromise. Mitigation: support key rotation, revocation lists, and allow airgapped manual key revocation via operator runbook. Risk: Bandwidth blackout. Mitigation: support physical media seeding (detailed process in linked playbook).
open_questions: - What is minimum supported edge proxy feature set (mTLS, range requests, byte-range resuming)? - Should we mandate a specific manifest signing format (COSE vs JWS vs simple detached signature)? - Do we require us to host a 'staging mirror image' offering for low-connectivity customers or leave entirely customer-hosted?
